title: What a town or state government is actually working on at any moment, and how fast those matters move
usableAnswer: A realistic catalog of recurring local and state matters by government type (zoning, budgets, contracts, ordinances, appointments) with typical durations, and evidence on how often public comment changes a proposal.
whyItMatters: The living world's background news is four local subjects and two international ones, cycling forever on invented gaps. At main 9f42ba19: src/simulation/living-world/developments.ts:43-81 — stage gaps of 6-18 days; :131 — a new matter every 20-45 days; :89-114 — the four and two subjects; :577-583 — the next outcome is an even random pick and any public comment always produces a revised proposal. None of these is marked or has a question. The answered built-producers-with-no-player-entry says to wire these matters to the player; this asks what they should contain.

answer.summary: Separate legislative matters, appropriations, contract review and appointments; the D.C. rules have distinct procedures rather than one matter timer. Official bill/agenda histories provide observed dates; elapsed time cannot be equated to mandatory legal waiting time.
